i support the idea, but these things aren't as easy as you're amking them out to be. First of all, there have to be tools written to decompile the archives for the game, and extract the relevant files (like character textures) Every game engine uses different methods of building these archives with different structures etc, so not one will be the same, no one-size-fits-all

secondly, you need to be able to re-inject said image back into the archive, which is tricky because often the game checks wether or not these archives have been modified in anyway, or simply not loading unsigned files.

Then on top of that there's also 'cheat detection' in a lot of games, that also independently verify any edited files. and that's just basic extraction and injection, doesnt even include compatibility, it's simple enough to replace a texture, it's a WHOLE other deal to replace a mesh, doubly so, a character, since there's SO much more information in those, that all needs to be in the right place where the game wants it to be for it to work, stuff like skinning weights, animation info, vertex colours etc.

THAT SAID, there's -plenty- of games that get cracked wide open within days, or at least weeks, so all these things are completely possible. Honestly, i was thinking of a similar idea myself, also because of the LOTR shite.
